## 1. Install the client

The client packages are the same in R and Python: same functions, same column names. Source and starter notebooks are on [GitHub](https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/aefsim).

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R
```r
install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("advanced-empirical-finance/aefsim/r")
```
## Python
```sh
uv add "git+https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/aefsim#subdirectory=python"
# or: pip install "git+https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/aefsim#subdirectory=python"
```
:::

## 2. Store your token

Your team receives one token, starting with `aef_`. Treat it like a password: it lets anyone trade for your team. Keep it out of your code and your Git repository by storing it in the environment variable `AEF_TOKEN`.

- **R:** add `AEF_TOKEN=aef_...` to `~/.Renviron` (`usethis::edit_r_environ()` opens the file), then restart R.
- **Python:** `export AEF_TOKEN=aef_...` in your shell, or put it in a `.env` file that you never commit.

## 3. Make a first submission

::: {.panel-tabset}
## R
```r
library(aefsim)
universe <- get_universe()                   # the stocks you can buy after the latest close
close_date <- max(universe$close_date)       # the close your decision is based on
get_parameters()                             # the rules; applies_next marks the current ones

weights <- tibble::tibble(ticker = c("AAPL", "MSFT", "JNJ"), weight = c(0.2, 0.2, 0.1))
validate(weights, close_date = close_date)   # every check, nothing stored
submit(weights, close_date = close_date,
       rationale = "Three large caps, half the book in cash while we learn the ropes.")
```
## Python
```python
import aefsim
import polars as pl
universe = aefsim.get_universe()             # a polars DataFrame
close_date = universe["close_date"].max()
aefsim.get_parameters()

weights = pl.DataFrame({"ticker": ["AAPL", "MSFT", "JNJ"], "weight": [0.2, 0.2, 0.1]})
aefsim.validate(weights, close_date=close_date)
aefsim.submit(weights, close_date=close_date,
              rationale="Three large caps, half the book in cash while we learn the ropes.")
```
:::

The check and the submission show the trade date: the next market open whose 09:00 New York deadline has not passed.

The [starter notebooks](https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/aefsim/tree/main/notebooks) take a full example from prices to submission: they download a year of prices with tidyfinance, pick the 20 least volatile S&P 500 stocks, then validate and submit.

## 4. The next morning

```r
get_submissions()     # status, trade date, rationale, weights
get_portfolio()       # one row: portfolio value, cash and the positions
get_performance()     # your daily portfolio value and statistics, next to the benchmarks
get_leaderboard()     # every team under its pseudonym
```

Your team's [dashboard](dashboard.qmd) shows the same in charts.

## When something goes wrong

Every message says what went wrong and what to do, and ends with a code in brackets. A rejected submission lists every problem at once. The most common ones:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `close_date_in_future` | `close_date` is later than the close before your trade. The message names the date to use. |
| `unknown_ticker` | Not a stock in the simulation. It uses Yahoo tickers, for example `BRK-B`. |
| `ineligible_ticker` | Closed below $5. You may hold or reduce such a position, but not add to it. |
| `short_not_allowed` | A negative weight before shorting opens on 5 April. |
| `leverage_exceeded`, `net_exposure_exceeded` | The sum of absolute weights, or of weights, is above the limit. |
| `too_many_positions` | More than 50 non-zero weights. |
| `rationale_missing` | Every submission needs a rationale. |
| `missing_token`, `unknown_token` | No token was found, or the server does not know it: check `AEF_TOKEN`. |

The [aefsim README](https://github.com/advanced-empirical-finance/aefsim#when-something-goes-wrong) explains every code.
